issues.title: Configurable New User Access Request Workflow for PULSE with Org Owner Routing, Remedy BI Option, and Unit Test Coverage
issues.description:
## Summary

Today, new user access requests follow the existing Remedy BI approach. This ticket must preserve that capability while introducing a new direct approval option that allows organization owners to receive and process access requests without using Remedy BI.

The solution must support two access request methods:

1. Existing Remedy BI workflow
2. New direct org owner approval workflow implemented within PULSE

Both methods must be available as configuration options, but only one method may be enabled for a given organization at a time.

A new capability must be added to the PULSE admin area so that organization owners and administrators can configure which access request method an organization uses. If the organization selects the new direct org owner approval method, the configuration must also allow the organization to select which org owner users will receive access request emails.

When the direct org owner approval method is enabled, a new user must be able to submit an access request from within PULSE for a specific organization. That request must generate an email to the configured org owner recipients. Email delivery must use the existing helper currently used for record creation and record update notifications, and it must rely on the existing application email configuration rather than introducing a separate email configuration model.

After receiving the email, the organization owner will review the request and then complete the approval process in PULSE by creating the user and assigning the appropriate permissions. This ticket does not require email-based approval actions; email is used for notification and routing, while approval completion remains in PULSE.

The work also includes documenting workflow options, reviewing them with stakeholders, confirming the agreed approach, and implementing the configuration and request-routing behavior. Unit tests must be added for all new business logic, configuration rules, and request handling paths.

## Business Need

PULSE needs a flexible and organization-specific approach for handling new user access requests. Some organizations may continue using the current Remedy BI workflow, while others need a simpler direct routing model that notifies organization owners and lets them complete onboarding directly within PULSE. The application must support both patterns without ambiguity and with clear administrative control.

## Functional Requirements

* Document and review the available workflow options for new user access requests.
* Support both the existing Remedy BI method and a new direct org owner approval method.
* Add admin functionality so organization owners and administrators can configure the access request method for an organization.
* Enforce that only one access request method can be active for an organization at any time.
* If the direct org owner approval method is selected, allow configuration of the org owner users who will receive request notification emails.
* Allow users to submit an access request from within PULSE for a specific organization.
* Route submitted requests according to the selected organization-level configuration.
* If Remedy BI is selected, preserve the current Remedy BI behavior.
* If direct org owner approval is selected, send the access request email to the configured org owner recipients.
* Use the existing email helper already used for record create/update notifications.
* Use the existing application email configuration for sending access request emails.
* Allow organization owners and administrators to manage the configuration for this capability.
* Require organization owners to complete approval by creating the user in PULSE and assigning the appropriate permissions.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Workflow options for new user access requests are documented and reviewed with stakeholders, including the existing Remedy BI flow and the new direct org owner approval flow.
* A final workflow design is agreed upon by the team and supports both methods as selectable organization-level options.
* A configuration option is available in the PULSE admin section for organization owners and administrators to select the access request method for an organization.
* The system enforces that only one access request method can be enabled for an organization at a time.
* The existing Remedy BI workflow remains supported for organizations configured to use it.
* A new direct org owner approval workflow is available for organizations configured to use it.
* When the direct org owner approval workflow is enabled, organization owners and administrators can configure which org owner users receive access request emails.
* A user can submit an access request from within PULSE for a specific organization.
* When a request is submitted for an organization using the Remedy BI method, the existing Remedy BI behavior is executed.
* When a request is submitted for an organization using the direct org owner approval method, an email notification is sent to the configured org owner recipients.
* Access request email notifications use the existing helper currently used for record creation and update emails.
* Access request email notifications use the existing email configuration already supported by the application.
* Organization owners can review the request and complete the approval process in PULSE by creating the user and assigning the appropriate permissions.
* Administrators retain the ability to configure and manage either workflow option.
* The feature is tested in development and staging before production deployment.
* Unit test coverage is added for all new logic introduced by this feature.

## Unit Test Requirements

Unit tests must be added or updated to cover the new workflow behavior and configuration rules, including at minimum:

* Organization-level selection of access request method.
* Validation that only one method can be active per organization at a time.
* Default and persisted configuration behavior for organizations.
* Authorization rules for who can configure the access request method.
* Authorization rules for who can configure direct-method recipients.
* Validation that configured direct-method recipients are valid org owner users.
* Access request submission behavior when an organization is configured for Remedy BI.
* Access request submission behavior when an organization is configured for direct org owner approval.
* Email notification dispatch for the direct org owner approval path.
* Use of the existing email helper for sending direct-method notifications.
* Handling of missing or invalid recipient configuration for the direct method.
* Any controller, service, or workflow branching logic added to support the two-method model.
* Regression coverage to confirm the existing Remedy BI path continues to function as expected.

## Out of Scope

* Email-based approve or deny actions directly from the email.
* Automatic user creation from the email workflow.
* Supporting multiple active access request methods for the same organization.
* Replacing the existing application-wide email configuration model.

## Notes

The direct org owner approval workflow is a routing and notification capability. Final approval and user provisioning still occur within PULSE, where the organization owner creates the user and assigns permissions.

issues.title: feat: Bulk select and bulk delete on the action list view
issues.description:
## Summary

Customers with many actions have no efficient way to remove them — deletion is strictly one action at a time (Edit page `#deleteBtn`, or the per-row bin icon that only appears on the Draft view). Add a checkbox multi-select to the action list with a **Bulk Delete** action so a user can select several rows and delete them in one operation. This is the lighter-lift half of a broader clean-up effort (see the retention-setting ticket).

## Current behavior (reference)

- List view: `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/List/Index.cshtml` (table `id="OneNListItems-Actions-table"`).
- Single-item delete: `ItemController.Delete(int id, string actionStatus)` — `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/ItemController.cs:1130`, which calls `IStoredProcedureService.DeleteOneNListItem(oneNListId, username)` (soft-delete to status Deleted=1749) and redirects to `~/List/Index?actionStatus=...`.
- No checkbox/select-all markup exists anywhere in `Views/List/`.

## Files to modify

- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/List/Index.cshtml` — add a leading checkbox column, a header "select all" checkbox, and a Bulk Delete button (hidden/disabled until ≥1 row is checked). Show a confirmation dialog (reuse the `DeleteRecordConfirmation()` JS pattern) with the count of selected rows.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/ItemController.cs` — add a new POST action `BulkDelete(int[] ids, string actionStatus)` mirroring `Delete`: validate ownership/authorization, iterate the ids calling `DeleteOneNListItem` per id (same soft-delete path), set `SessionManager.SuccessMessage` (e.g. "N actions were deleted successfully."), redirect back to `~/List/Index?actionStatus=...`. Guard against an empty selection.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/wwwroot/scripts/` — JS to wire select-all, per-row toggle, enable/disable the Bulk Delete button, and post the selected ids.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each row on the action list has a selection checkbox; a header checkbox selects/deselects all visible rows.
- [ ] A Bulk Delete button is disabled until at least one row is selected.
- [ ] Clicking Bulk Delete shows a confirmation dialog stating how many actions will be deleted; cancelling makes no changes.
- [ ] Confirming deletes all selected actions via the existing `DeleteOneNListItem` soft-delete path and returns to the same list view with a success message reflecting the count.
- [ ] Bulk delete respects the same authorization as single delete; a user cannot delete actions they could not delete individually.
- [ ] Bulk select/delete works on every status view (Recent, Draft, Pre-Award, etc.), not only Draft.
- [ ] Project builds with no errors or warnings after the change.
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass.

## Unit Test Requirements

- `ItemController.BulkDelete_WithSelectedIds_DeletesEachAndRedirects` — asserts `DeleteOneNListItem` is invoked once per id and the result redirects to `List/Index` with the correct `actionStatus`.
- `ItemController.BulkDelete_WithEmptySelection_DeletesNothingAndReturns` — asserts no delete calls occur and the user is returned to the list without error.

issues.title: feat: Success message states when an action was created as a draft
issues.description:
## Summary

New PULSE users think their actions disappear after creating them, because every new action is persisted in **Draft** status and the default list view ("Recent") does not show drafts. The generic success message "Action Created successfully." does not tell them the action is a draft. Update the create success message to clearly state that the action was created in a **draft** status and how to find/advance it, reducing confusion and duplicate creation.

## Current behavior (reference)

- Every new action is persisted as Draft (72) first — `ItemController.BuildNewActionItem()` (`Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/ItemController.cs:151`, sets `fk_ActionStatus_Lookup_ID = eActionStatus.Draft`).
- On `POST Create`, `SessionManager.SuccessMessage = "Action Created successfully.";` (`ItemController.cs:327`) then redirects to `~/Item/Edit?Id={id}`.
- Draft enum: `Enumerations.eActionStatus.Draft = 72`.

## Files to modify

- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/ItemController.cs` — in `POST Create`, when the saved action's status is Draft, set a clear message, e.g. "Action created as a **Draft**. Drafts are not shown on the Recent list — open the **Draft** view to find it or advance it to Pre-Award." Keep the existing message for non-draft saves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Creating an action that lands in Draft status shows a success message that explicitly says the action is a draft and how to locate it (Draft view).
- [ ] Creating/saving an action that is not in Draft status keeps the existing standard success message.
- [ ] The message renders through the existing `SessionManager.SuccessMessage` channel (no new alert mechanism).
- [ ] Project builds with no errors or warnings after the change.
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass.

## Unit Test Requirements

- `ItemController.Create_ActionSavedAsDraft_SetsDraftAwareSuccessMessage` — asserts the draft-specific message is set when status is Draft (72).
- `ItemController.Create_ActionSavedAsNonDraft_SetsStandardSuccessMessage` — asserts the standard message for non-draft status.

issues.title: feat: Return to the Draft list view after creating a draft action
issues.description:
## Summary

Companion to the draft success-message ticket. Because new actions are saved as Draft and the list defaults to "Recent" (which excludes drafts), users returning to the list do not see the action they just created and often create a duplicate. When a user has just created/closed an action that is in Draft status, the list should open on the **Draft** view (showing the just-created action) instead of always defaulting to Recent.

## Current behavior (reference)

- `ListController.Index` defaults `actionStatus` to `eListActionStatus.Recent` when no status param is supplied (`Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/ListController.cs:95`).
- "Recent" filters to statuses 73/74/75 in `OneNListItemService.QueryForList` (`Source/OneNListApp.Service/OneNListItemService.cs:158`), so Draft (72) actions never appear in the default view.
- After create, `ItemController` redirects to `~/Item/Edit?Id={id}`; navigating back to the list uses the Recent default.
- The list already fully supports a Draft view (`?actionStatus=Draft`), including a per-row delete icon.

## Approach

When the user closes/returns to the list from a just-created Draft action, land them on `~/List/Index?actionStatus=Draft`. Prefer driving this off the created action's status (route the "return to list"/close link to the Draft view when the action is a Draft) rather than permanently changing the global default, so the Recent default is preserved for normal navigation.

## Files to modify

- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/ItemController.cs` and/or `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/Item/Edit.cshtml` — make the "return to list"/close navigation target `actionStatus=Draft` when the current action's status is Draft (72).
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/ListController.cs` — no change to the global Recent default; ensure the Draft view renders correctly when linked to directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After creating an action that is in Draft status, closing/returning to the list opens the **Draft** view with that action visible.
- [ ] Normal navigation to the list (not coming from a just-created draft) still defaults to the Recent view.
- [ ] The Draft view continues to show the per-row delete icon and correct columns.
- [ ] No duplicate action is created when a user follows the create → close → list flow.
- [ ] Project builds with no errors or warnings after the change.
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass.

## Unit Test Requirements

- `ItemController.Create_DraftAction_ReturnLinkTargetsDraftView` — asserts the close/return target carries `actionStatus=Draft` for a Draft action.
- `ListController.Index_ActionStatusDraft_ReturnsDraftStatusItems` — asserts the Draft status view queries Draft (72) items (guards the existing default is unchanged for Recent).

issues.title: Add security-group visibility/access flags for OrbitalLink and FieldSat actions, mirroring existing Baymark/Northline behavior
issues.description:
Implement security-group-based visibility/access for actions where `IsStarshieldAction` and/or `IsmVSATAction` are checked, using the same pattern that already exists for `HasCHSAccess` and `HasNorthlineAccess`.

Today, org owners can enable `Baymark` and `Northline` cross-access per user group from Admin \> User Groups, and the SQL permission functions use those flags to expand record visibility. `FieldSat` and `OrbitalLink` action fields already exist on actions, but their original migrations explicitly scoped out access flags, read-only enforcement, and list-view filtering. As a result, org owners currently cannot grant specific groups visibility to `FieldSat` or `OrbitalLink` actions the way they can for `Baymark` and `Northline`.

**Required changes**

1. Add two new nullable permission columns to `dbo.Organization_Security_Group` in a new idempotent migration.\
   Use exact names consistently across SQL, EF, viewmodels, tests, and UI. Preferred names:\
   `HasStarshieldAccess`\
   `HasmVSATAccess`\
   Do not modify historical migrations under `Previous_Migrations`; add a new forward migration under the current migration versioning pattern.
2. Update the data model and EF mapping for the new columns.\
   Files likely involved:\
   `Source/OneNListApp.Data/Models/Organization_Security_Group.cs`\
   `Source/OneNListApp.Data/OneNListContext.cs`
3. Update the Admin user-group edit/create flow so org owners can enable these flags per group.\
   Add the new properties to `SecurityGroupViewModel`.\
   Add new checkboxes to the PM/Limited behavior section of the user-group form beside the existing `Northline` and `Baymark` toggles.\
   Persist values on create/edit and reload them correctly on GET/edit.
4. Update permission SQL so these flags actually grant action visibility.\
   In both:\
   `dbo.fnGetOneNListIDsUserHasPermissionsFor`\
   `dbo.BO_fnGetOneNListUserHasPermissionsFor`\
   extend the PM / Financials Limited branch to:\
   compute the new flags with OR semantics across all assigned security groups\
   union in all actions where `OneNList.IsmVSATAction = 1` when `HasmVSATAccess = 1`\
   union in all actions where `OneNList.IsStarshieldAction = 1` when `HasStarshieldAccess = 1`\
   Keep the two TVFs in lock-step just like the existing Baymark/Northline logic.
5. Ensure detail-page access matches list visibility.\
   A user who can see an action in the list because of the new flag must also be able to open that action in item/detail flows.\
   A user without the new flag must not gain access to `FieldSat`/`OrbitalLink` actions just because those checkboxes are selected.\
   Verify whether `GetOneNListItemById` and related access paths already inherit TVF behavior; if not, update the relevant SQL path so list/detail behavior stays consistent.
6. Mirror the current restricted-action behavior, not just the list filter.\
   If Baymark/Northline parity today includes read-only/edit gating for restricted actions, extend that same behavior to `FieldSat` and `OrbitalLink`.\
   Important: do not copy the current “first security group only” fallback from `GeneralReadOnlyHelper`. Visibility TVFs already use OR semantics across all assigned groups, so any new helper logic must also evaluate all assigned groups with OR semantics.
7. Do not seed any group enabled by default unless product/business explicitly provides a seed list.\
   Default behavior should remain disabled for existing groups until an org owner enables it.

**Why**

This closes a gap in the current feature set. `OrbitalLink` and `FieldSat` are already modeled as action-level checkbox fields, but unlike `Baymark`/`Northline`, there is no per-group configuration to let org owners grant visibility/access for those actions. The result is inconsistent behavior across similar action classification flags and forces manual workarounds.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. In Admin \> User Groups, org owners can see and save two new toggles for eligible groups:\
   `OrbitalLink Cross-Access`\
   `FieldSat Cross-Access`
2. The new flag values persist in `Organization_Security_Group` and reload correctly on edit.
3. A user assigned to any security group with `HasStarshieldAccess = 1` can see and open actions where `IsStarshieldAction = 1`, even when the action is not otherwise visible through the group’s PMPD mapping.
4. A user assigned to any security group with `HasmVSATAccess = 1` can see and open actions where `IsmVSATAction = 1`, even when the action is not otherwise visible through the group’s PMPD mapping.
5. Multi-group users get OR semantics.\
   If any assigned group grants `OrbitalLink` access, the user gets `OrbitalLink` visibility.\
   If any assigned group grants `FieldSat` access, the user gets `FieldSat` visibility.\
   Do not rely on only the first assigned group.
6. Users without the relevant new flag do not gain visibility/access to `OrbitalLink` or `FieldSat` actions solely because those action checkboxes are set.
7. Existing `Baymark`, `Northline`, and `Region` behavior remains unchanged.
8. BI/report parity is maintained by updating both permission TVFs, not just the app-facing one.
9. A new forward-only migration is added; historical migration files are not edited.

**Testing requirements**

Add unit tests for the new flags in the same style as the existing `HasNorthlineAccess` / `HasCHSAccess` coverage.

Minimum required test updates:\
`OneNListApp.Tests/Web/UserGroupControllerTests.cs`\
`OneNListApp.Tests/Service/SecurityGroupServiceTests.cs`\
`OneNListApp.Tests/Infrastructure/TestBuilders.cs`

Add tests that verify:\
GET edit maps the new entity flags to the viewmodel\
POST create/edit maps the new viewmodel flags back to the entity\
false values persist as false, not null, when explicitly unchecked\
default/null behavior remains safe for older rows

If read-only/helper behavior is updated, add unit tests for that helper covering:\
user with no matching flag on any group remains restricted\
user with the matching flag on one assigned group is allowed\
multi-group case where first group is false and second group is true still grants access

If the repo’s SQL integration harness can support it, also add or extend an integration test proving the permission TVF returns `IsStarshieldAction = 1` / `IsmVSATAction = 1` records when the corresponding group flag is enabled. Since the core visibility logic lives in SQL migrations, integration coverage is strongly preferred in addition to unit tests.

issues.title: Improve Admin PM/PdM lookup management by showing assigned PdMs and replacing PdM Parent ID with a PM dropdown
issues.description:
Current admin maintenance of PM/PdM relationships is difficult and error-prone. Today, a user must know the PM lookup item ID and then manually open individual PdM/PdD lookup items to inspect or update their `parentId`. In the current implementation, `PdMPdD` and `PMPD` lookup items still render the `parentId` field as a numeric textbox, and the read-only view shows the raw numeric ID instead of the related PM name.

As part of `PULSE v5.1.7`, update the Admin lookup item experience so PM/PdM relationships are visible and manageable without requiring lookup IDs:

* Replace the `PdMPdD` `Parent ID` numeric textbox with a dropdown of active PM (`PMPD`) lookup items for the current organization.
* Show the selected PM name in read-only/view mode instead of the raw numeric `parentId`.
* When viewing or editing a PM (`PMPD`) lookup item, display the assigned PdM/PdD children by name so admins can immediately see which PdMs belong to that PM.
* Apply the same parent-selection experience to the create flow, not just edit, since \[CreateForLookup.cshtml (line 1)\](C:/Users/1392121133121005.CTR/Repositories/PULSE/pulse/Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/Views/LookupItem/CreateForLookup.cshtml:1) currently does not render a parent selector at all.
* Keep the existing `ProgramSupportedByAction` parent-dropdown behavior intact.

Implementation notes from code review:

* `LookupItemController.PopulateEditViewData()` already builds a PM dropdown list that can be reused/expanded.
* The app already has relationship retrieval available through `IStoredProcedureService.GetChildrenLookupsFor(...)`.
* The existing `GetPMPDLookupsWithPdMs` helper appears intended for item-form filtering and is not suitable for admin display as-is because it emits ID-based select text/value pairs rather than admin-friendly names.

**Unit Tests**\
Add or update unit tests to cover:

* `LookupItemController.Edit()` for a `PdMPdD` item populates `ParentIdDropDownList` with active PMs for the current org only.
* `LookupItemController.Edit()` for a `PMPD` item populates assigned child PdM/PdD values for display.
* `LookupItemController.CreateForLookup()` for `PdMPdD` populates the same PM dropdown.
* Posting `Edit` for `PdMPdD` persists the selected PM lookup item ID to `LookupItem.parentId`.
* Posting `CreateForLookup` for `PdMPdD` persists the selected PM lookup item ID to `LookupItem.parentId`.
* Regression guard: inactive or out-of-org PMs are not shown in the dropdown.
* Regression guard: existing `ProgramSupportedByAction` parent dropdown behavior is unchanged.

**Acceptance Criteria**

* In Admin, opening a `PdM/PdD` lookup item shows `Parent` as a dropdown of available active PMs, not a numeric textbox.
* The `PdM/PdD` create flow also shows the same PM dropdown.
* Saving a `PdM/PdD` item stores the selected PM relationship correctly in `parentId`.
* In read-only/view mode, a `PdM/PdD` item displays the parent PM name instead of the numeric parent ID.
* Opening a `PM/PD` lookup item shows the assigned `PdM/PdD` children by name, with a clear empty state when none are assigned.
* Only active PMs for the current organization appear in the dropdown.
* Existing parent-dropdown behavior for `Program Supported by Action` continues to work with no regression.

issues.title: Fix duplicate Prime Contractor lookup creation and restore post-save redirect in PULSE
issues.description:
A user added a new Prime Contractor and Vendor ID entry in PULSE for `Vertex Manufacturing Inc.`. After saving, the application did not return the user to the PULSE lookup/settings page. Instead, it displayed a raw JSON response in the browser:

`{"success":true,"reloadPage":true}`

Because the user remained on that response page and retried/refreshed multiple times, the system created the same Prime Contractor lookup entry three times.

The application does not allow true deletion of lookup items when they are referenced by related tables, so cleanup of the duplicate rows must be handled through a database script.

**Problem Statement**

There are two issues that need to be addressed:

1. Existing data issue:\
   Duplicate `Vertex Manufacturing Inc.` Prime Contractor lookup entries were created and must be cleaned up safely at the database level.
2. Application issue:\
   The lookup create flow is not handling the save/redirect experience correctly. Instead of navigating the user back to the appropriate PULSE page after a successful create, it leaves the user on a raw JSON response, which encourages refresh/retry behavior and results in duplicate inserts.

**Scope**

This work will be completed in two parts:

1. Database remediation\
   Create and execute a database script to identify the duplicate `Vertex Manufacturing Inc.` Prime Contractor lookup records, preserve the correct record, update related references as needed, and remove or deactivate the duplicate rows safely.
2. Application fix\
   Update the lookup item create/save flow so that after a successful create, the user is returned to the correct PULSE lookup/settings page and duplicate creation from refresh/retry is prevented.

**Technical Approach**

For the database cleanup:

* Identify the three `Vertex Manufacturing Inc.` Prime Contractor lookup records.
* Determine which record should be retained as the source-of-truth record.
* Update foreign key references in related tables from the duplicate records to the retained record.
* Remove, deactivate, or otherwise retire the two duplicate records in a way that preserves referential integrity.
* Validate that only one usable `Vertex Manufacturing Inc.` Prime Contractor lookup remains after the script runs.

For the application fix:

* Review the controller/action and client-side behavior used by lookup item creation.
* Correct the save response handling so the user is redirected or reloaded into the proper PULSE page instead of being shown raw JSON.
* Add protection against duplicate inserts caused by browser refresh/replay or repeated submission after a successful create.
* Confirm the fix applies to this lookup workflow and does not regress other lookup create/edit behaviors that use the same pattern.

**Acceptance Criteria**

1. A database cleanup script is created for the duplicate `Vertex Manufacturing Inc.` Prime Contractor lookup entries.
2. The script preserves one valid `Vertex Manufacturing Inc.` record and safely remaps any related table references from the two duplicate records.
3. After the cleanup is executed, only one active/usable `Vertex Manufacturing Inc.` Prime Contractor lookup entry remains in PULSE.
4. Creating a new Prime Contractor/Vendor ID lookup item no longer leaves the user on a raw JSON response page.
5. After a successful create, the user is returned to the correct PULSE lookup/settings screen.
6. Refreshing or retrying after a successful create does not create duplicate lookup entries.
7. The fix does not break editing existing lookup entries.
8. The fix does not regress other lookup create flows that share the same implementation pattern, if applicable.

**Unit Test Coverage**

1. Add a unit test verifying the lookup create action returns the expected redirect or navigation result for a successful browser-based create.
2. Add a unit test verifying the successful create flow does not render the raw JSON response as the end-user page in the normal workflow.
3. Add a unit test verifying a successful create inserts exactly one lookup record.
4. Add a unit test verifying repeated submission/replay handling does not create multiple identical lookup records for the same logical create event.
5. Add a unit test verifying the lookup list page loads correctly after create and includes the new value only once.
6. If database-script testing exists in this codebase, add coverage verifying duplicate references are remapped to the retained record before duplicate rows are retired.

**Definition of Done**

1. Database cleanup script is written, reviewed, and executed in the appropriate environment.
2. Duplicate `Vertex Manufacturing Inc.` records are resolved without orphaning related data.
3. Application code is updated to restore correct post-save navigation behavior.
4. Automated tests are added or updated for the create/redirect/duplicate-prevention flow.
5. QA confirms that creating a lookup item returns the user to the correct page and does not create duplicates on refresh/retry.
